downside.story: AI capex digestion: customer capex lands near the low case (CY2027 ~1.4T, CY2028 flat-to-down), MRVL loses a custom socket to Broadcom/MediaTek and custom mix compresses GM; P/E falls toward NVDA/CRDO levels (~15x) while the Lumentum overhang persists.

upside.story: Capex follows the high case (CY2027 ~2.4T), Google TPU attach and the key hyperscaler XPU ramp put FY2028 at or above the ~$20B outlook, scale-up optics adds; the sector re-rates to the snapshot peer median and the deal is seen as accretive.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex 22% below the base path (toward the standing file's low case: 2027 $1,390B, 2028 $1,265B) as the November AI selloff turns into budget cuts at labs and neoclouds; Marvell loses custom share (Trainium/Alchip, an XPU program slips) and module makers move DSP sockets to Broadcom/Credo after the Lumentum deal (Counterpoint): share -10%; GM -1.5pt on deleverage; P/E -6 turns on the after-SBC basis (~19.8x, ~16x on the peers' basis, at the CRDO/COHR end of today's peer range). Deal still pending with an overpaid LITE at peak optics.

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex near the file's high path (2027 ~$2.2T) as the Q4 calls put numbers on "significantly more" 2027 spend; Marvell reaches the Investor Day FY28 ~$20B and FY29 custom >$12B with 1.6T DSPs and scale-up optics (share +8%); GM +0.5pt; peer multiples recover from the November rout (+6 turns after SBC). The deal closes on schedule with laser-supply and $1B+ cost synergies and no material DSP customer loss.

downside.story: 10th percentile (~$71): the moratorium pledges bite and hyperscalers digest in CY2027-28 (AI capex 25% below my base, near the standing view's low case), Marvell content per capex dollar 8% lower (Trainium generation to Alchip, Microsoft dual-sources, module makers move DSP orders away from a Lumentum-owned Marvell), custom mix takes GM 2pt lower, the P/E de-rates 6 turns to 13.5x (NVDA traded ~10x at 2026-11-20) and the FCF yield widens 35% to 3.1%; the Lumentum deal stays pending at p 0.55.

upside.story: 90th percentile (~$329, near the 52-week high): AI capex 25% above my base (NVIDIA's $130B Q4 guide holds the cycle), share of wallet +8% (scale-up optics, Google TPU attach early), GM +1pt, the P/E re-rates 7 turns to 26.5x (back toward the unrepriced peer median) and the FCF yield tightens 20% to 1.84%.

downside.story: P10: an AI capex digestion starts in 2027 (standing file low case: 2027 $1,390B vs base $1,841B): customer capex -22% and Marvell's share of wallet -10% in every forecast quarter (custom programs slip, Trainium work to Alchip, Microsoft late), DC revenue ~30% below base; C&O -10%; GM -2pt on under-absorption, opex only -4%; AI semis de-rate further to ~13.8x NTM P/E and a ~2.7% FCF yield (NVDA already trades at 8.65x after its CEO exit). The Lumentum deal stays pending at the signed 4.5 ratio (adjustment unchanged).

upside.story: P90: toward the standing file high case (customer capex +15%) with Google TPU-attach programs and scale-up optics landing early (share of wallet +6%): FY28 revenue ~$23B, FY29 ~$34B; GM ~57.4%; the AI-infrastructure group re-rates back toward its late-October level (~30x NTM in the 2026-11-01 peer snapshot): MRVL ~29.8x and a ~1.5% FCF yield. Deal adjustment held at base (in this case the fixed ratio costs more, so the case is slightly generous).

downside.story: P10: AI capex digestion: Big-4 capex on the standing file's low path (2027 $880B, 2028 $800B, about -25% vs base over FY28-29), MRVL loses custom share (Google's MediaTek shift repeated at AWS/Microsoft), GM -1.5pt on lower utilisation and custom pricing; the exit P/E falls to ~12x (CRDO/COHR today; NVDA trades 8x). Recession odds 21% (Kalshi-style 2027 market) and data-center moratorium pledges after the midterms make this a 1-in-10 outcome, not a tail.

upside.story: P90: capex on the standing file's high path (2027 $1,360B, 2028 $1,750B), custom programs reach the investor-day trajectory (>$12B FY29), GM holds the H2 FY27 range, and the multiple re-rates to ~24.6x (ALAB/AMD today, where MRVL traded before the deal) as deal fears fade.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex digestion toward the standing file low case (customer capex -20% vs base every forecast quarter), Marvell share of wallet -10% (custom ramps slip a year; optical-DSP share lost to Broadcom/Credo if module makers react to a Marvell-Lumentum combination), gross margin -1.5pt; P/E -9 turns (8.0x on the 17.0x base). Lumentum deal at its expected-value weight (p 0.75); a signed deal with a large DSP customer backlash is one path into this case.

upside.story: 90th percentile: customer capex +12% vs base, share of wallet +8% (custom >$12B FY29 as targeted, Google TPU-attach, scale-up optics), gross margin +0.5pt, P/E +5 turns (22.0x on the 17.0x base). Lumentum deal (signed) at its expected-value weight; full synergy capture at Inphi pace is one path into this case.
